title: ALLEN ARREST
full_story:
On Wednesday, at approximately 3:28 pm the Clay County Sheriff’s Office received a report of a domestic disturbance at a residence on Persimmon Drive.  The reported suspect had multiple outstanding felony warrants, a history of flight, a history of violence, and it had also been reported that he was possibly in possession of a firearm recently.  While deputies were responding to the residence, they received information that the suspect had fled on foot.  The drone was deployed and the suspect was located immediately in a nearby field.  Due to the dry conditions deputies were able to drive across the field to approach the suspect in their squad cars.  The suspect was attempting to flee and continued to do so when the deputies encountered him in the field.  The suspect was given orders to stop, or he would be bit by a K-9.  The suspect ignored the orders and continued to run.  K-9 Chief was released and was commanded to apprehend the suspect, which was successful.  The suspect was taken into custody and continued to resist deputies when they were attempting to place him in the squad car.  The suspect received minor cuts and scratches from his encounter with the K-9, and received treatment from EMS and was later transported to a local hospital per office policy.

As a result of this incident and ongoing investigations by the Flora Police Department, Hunter D. Allen, 25, of Flora, was arrested on Clay County Warrants, for the offenses of Burglary, Theft less than $500, Possession of Another person’s Debit Card, 2 counts of Fleeing or Attempting to Elude a Police Officer, and 2 new charges of Resisting Arrest.  Allen is currently incarcerated in the Clay County Jail awaiting his first appearance in court.

The charge is merely an accusation, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

title: FIRST PROPERTY TAX PAYMENT DUE
full_story:
The first installment of the 2025 payable 2026 Real Estate Tax Bill is due one week from today.  The Treasurer’s Office will be closed on Monday in observance of Columbus Day.  If you have questions about your tax bill, please feel free to call the Treasurer’s office.  If you cannot get through, please leave a message, and they will return your call as soon as possible.  Phone 618-665-3727.

Payment can be made to the Clay County Treasurer using any of the following options, by mail send your check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville, IL 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.

At the treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse where they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money order.  Bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  Office hours are 8:00-4:00 Monday through Friday, but closed on national holidays.

Online by credit/debit card: Go to www.govpaynow.com PLC #a00082.

Or by drop box at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.

title: LOUISVILLE FALL HARVEST FESTIVAL
full_story:
The 75th Annual Louisville Fall Harvest Festival will start on Friday, October 30th.

Orders for Louisville Chamber of Commerce whole smoked pork loins can be purchased until October 25th, with pork loins to be picked up at Salt & Strings Butchery on November10th from 4 to 7 pm.

The Kiddie Parade kicks things off at 2 pm, with Full Armor Christian School serving treats at the old Soda Fountain and the Red Brush Christian Church will be serving apple cider and the Louisville Christian Church will be serving free water near the pocket park.  From 4 to 6 pm the Methodist Church will be offering free chili with Das-zle Dance and tumble performing at 5:30 pm.  From 5:30 to 6:30 pm will be the past Queen reception at the State Bank Suite.  At 6:15 pm Sylvia and Meila Robey will sing on stage.  The Little Miss, JR Miss, and Queen pageants will be held at 7:00 pm and the glow 5K walk, run will take place after the pageants.  From 9 to 10 pm there will be music on the square with Seth Schnautz.

Saturday starts with the Rotary Pancake breakfast at 7 am, with tickets now on sale.  The FFA, AG Mechanics Tractor show will be on the east side of the square and kids activities will start at 8 am and the Clay County Genealogical Society Library will have an open house.  The Clay County Cruisers Car Show begins at 9, there will also be a greased pig contest, sponsored by the Hoosier Prairie Baptist Church, and a country store will open at the old Clay County Jail with free coffee and popcorn.

The Princess pageant will be on the main stage at 10 am with special guest Briley Mullins performing.  Starting at 11 am will be the Chili Cook Off Contest, hosted by the North Clay FCCLA and the Louisville Chamber of Commerce, with tastings available to 1 pm.  Contestants should bring their chili to the pocket park by 10:45 am.  Sign up by emailing [email protected], the winner will get a $50 prize.  At 11:30 Power and Grace Tumbling will perform on the main stage.  At 1 pm Deputy Trevin Smith and his K9 Chief will have a demonstration.  The parade is at 2 pm followed by the crowning of the Queens and the Rotary Basket Raffle winners will be announced.

For the Parade floats, cars, tractors, bands and Queens will line up at the grade school, horses will line up at the city park, Louisville Queens and contestants will line up on Magnolia Street, and Emergency Services will line up at the high school.  Handicap parking for the parade will be available on the east side of the square.

All weekend there will be arts, and crafts, food vendors, basket raffle and inflatables for the kids.

In conjunction with the Fall Harvest Festival Red Brush Christian Church will have a Trunk or Treat on Wednesday, October 28th from 6 to 7:30 pm, and the Louisville American Legion will have a meat shoot on Sunday, November 1st at 11 am.

title: BODY FOUND AT REST AREA
full_story:
On Wednesday at 8:34 am, the Illinois State Police were contacted by the Illinois Department of Transportation workers who advised them that they found an unresponsive male lying outside his vehicle at the rest area on I-70 between Effingham and Altamont.

Effingham County Coroner Kim Rhodes responded to the rest area and pronounced the individual deceased at 9:10 am.  He was identified as Bradley D. Boisen, age 60 of New Holland, Pennsylvania.  There were no obvious injuries and no foul play is suspected.

Mr. Boisen was transported to the Effingham County Morgue where next of kin were notified.  His family advised he did not have a primary doctor and were not sure of his medical history.  An autopsy is scheduled today in Olney to determine the official cause of death.

The death remains under investigation by the Effingham County Coroner’s Office and the Illinois State Police.

Agencies on scene were the Illinois Department of Transportation, Illinois State Police, Illinois State Police Crime Scene Services, Rural Med EMS and the Effingham County Coroners Office.

The rest area has been closed for several years and currently is being renovated buy IDOT.

title: BYERS ACCIDENT
full_story:
Craig E. Byers, 47, of Louisville, was taken to Clay County Hospital after his 2015 Chevy left the road and landed on a creek embankment at about 5:40 pm Tuesday.

Byers was driving north on County Highway 13 when his vehicle left the roadway and became airborne over a creek near County Road 2200 North in Garden Hill Township in Wayne County.  The vehicle landed on its top on the north side of the creek and then began to roll.  The vehicle was totaled, according to county reports.

title: PILOT LOAN PROGRAM
full_story:
A pilot loan program designed to help Illinois farmers invest in on-farm grain storage was unveiled Wednesday by Governor JB Pritzker and the Illinois Finance Authority (IFA).

“Today we are taking an important step to assist farmers in these very challenging times,” Pritzker said during his Wednesday visit to Halpin Cattle Farms in Gardner.  “We’re launching low-interest loans for farmers to help them finance infrastructure like grain storage facilities, helping farmers to expand capacity and to navigate this very difficult market.”

Pritzker later shared more details in a press release explaining the benefits of on-farm storage, explaining it can reduce transportation, handling and storage costs while giving farmers greater flexibility in marketing their grain.

The pilot program is expected to offer loans at a 2% interest rate with the overall goal of lowering financing costs for farmers investing in grain storage and related equipment.  According to a resolution from IFA, the program will utilize up to $2 million in existing agricultural loan guarantee funds.

During the farm visit, Pritzker also discussed his administration’s efforts to expand international trade partnerships, including agreements signed with Mexico and Indonesia in the past year.  He further highlighted an October 6th executive order allowing farmers to use red-dyed diesel in agricultural vehicles off the farm, noting diesel costs have increased 140% since February.

“Illinois farmers don’t want any handouts; they just want a fair shot at making a buck.  They want stable markets.  They want reasonable input costs.  They want a chance to make a living, and I’m very proud as governor to have their backs,” Pritzker said.

For more information about the loan program, email IFA Senior Vice President Francisco Galliano at [email protected].

title: CHINESE NATIONAL SENTENCED
full_story:
A district judge sentenced a Chinese national to 27 months in federal prison for acting as a courier in an investment scam.

Shenghan Jin, 27, plead guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of wire fraud.

“A Chinese national who should have been gone in 2022 was still here in 2025, abusing our immigration system and helping fleece a Belleville man of his life savings.  After Jin finishes his well-deserved prison sentence, he will be immediately deported,” said US Attorney Steven D. Weinhoeft.

Uncharged members of the conspiracy began speaking with the victim online in May 2024.  Court documents explain the conspirators gained the victim’s trust and then began discussing investment strategies and opportunities. Conspirators instructed the victim to wire money to fake accounts and purchase gold bars.  Jin was arrested when he arrived at the victim’s home to pick up the gold in July 2025.

“Anyone who is succeeds in using lies and tricks to lure seniors into phony investments deserves prison.  We count every fraudster who is caught and imprisoned a win for the American people,” said IRS Criminal Investigation Special Agent in Charge William Steenson of the Kansas City Field Office.

In total, the victim is estimated to have lost approximately $2.5 million through cryptocurrency, wire transfers and physical gold transactions.

Jin was in the country on a student visa that expired in 2022.  Following imprisonment, Jin will be deported.

IRS Criminal Investigation and the US Secret Service contributed to the investigation.  Assistant US Attorney Kathleen Howard prosecuted the case.
